prompt: Two forces act on an object at the origin of the standard (x,y) coordinate plane. One force has a magnitude of 40 newtons and points in the direction of the positive x-axis. The other force has a magnitude of 65 newtons and points in the direction 125° counterclockwise from the positive x-axis. To the nearest tenth of a newton, what is the magnitude of the resultant force (the vector sum of the two forces)?
explanation: The second force has components 65 cos 125° ≈ -37.28 and 65 sin 125° ≈ 53.24. The resultant is ⟨40 - 37.28, 53.24⟩ = ⟨2.72, 53.24⟩, with magnitude √(2.72² + 53.24²) ≈ 53.3 newtons. The option 66.6 leaves out the second force's horizontal component, using ⟨40, 53.24⟩. The option 39.6 writes 125° as 90° + 35° and swaps sine and cosine, giving the second force components -65 cos 35° and 65 sin 35°. The option 65.8 uses the law of cosines on the 55° angle of the force triangle but drops the factor 2: √(40² + 65² - 40·65·cos 55°).
quantity_asked: the magnitude of the sum of the two force vectors.

distractor_kind.66.6: error path: second force's horizontal component omitted. (a) not a parameter extreme. (b) not the colinear values 25 or 105. (c) the angle between the forces is obtuse, so 25 < R < √(40² + 65²) ≈ 76.3; strictly inside. (d) real component omission.
distractor_kind.39.6: error path: sine and cosine swapped after writing 125° = 90° + 35°. (a) no extreme. (b) not at an edge. (c) inside (25, 76.3). (d) real reference-angle error.
distractor_kind.65.8: error path: law of cosines without the factor 2. (a) no extreme. (b) not at an edge. (c) inside (25, 76.3). (d) real formula slip.

bounds: angle between the forces is obtuse (125°), so R < √(40² + 65²) ≈ 76.3
mechanism: resultant of two forces
vector components from direction angle
magnitude of a vector sum
obtuse angle between forces
arith_class_check: No. One-decimal values; nothing in the stem implies a class.
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 53.3 and 65.8, both two digits with one decimal; neither is rounder.

self_audit.note: Interior key; the obtuse-angle cap 76.3 and the 25 floor contain every option; 65.8 and 66.6 are a near pair that does not include the key.

subskill: scalar multiple and difference of matrices, 2 × 2 determinant
prompt: Matrix A has first row (6, 4) and second row (4, 6). Matrix B has first row (−1, 4) and second row (−2, 1). What is the determinant of the matrix 2A − B ?
explanation: 2A has rows (12, 8) and (8, 12). Subtracting B entry by entry gives 2A − B with rows (12 − (−1), 8 − 4) = (13, 4) and (8 − (−2), 12 − 1) = (10, 11). Its determinant is 13(11) − 4(10) = 143 − 40 = 103. The option 73 treats the determinant as if it distributed over subtraction: det(2A) − det(B) = 4(20) − 7 = 73. The option 33 also forgets that doubling every entry of a 2 × 2 matrix multiplies the determinant by 4: 2(20) − 7 = 33. The option 81 takes 12 − (−1) as 11, so the first row is (11, 4) and the determinant is 121 − 40 = 81.
quantity_asked: det(2A − B), the determinant of the 2 × 2 matrix 2A − B.

distractor_kind.33: error path: det(2A − B) taken as 2 det A − det B (determinant treated as linear in the whole matrix). (a) no extreme. (b) not at an edge. (c) inside. (d) real misconception, the scalar not squared.
distractor_kind.73: error path: det(2A − B) taken as det(2A) − det(B), with det(2A) = 4 det A done correctly. (a) no parameter extreme. (b) neighbouring setup (the difference of the two determinants) — not a bound on the key; inside. (c) no one-step estimate bounds a determinant of a difference; inside. (d) real 'determinant is linear' misconception.
distractor_kind.81: error path: sign slip 12 − (−1) = 11 in entry (1, 1). (a) no extreme. (b) not an intermediate at an edge. (c) inside. (d) real subtraction-of-a-negative slip.

bounds: none forced: the entries of 2A − B mix signs, so the stem bounds the determinant on neither side
mechanism: determinant of 2A − B
scalar multiple and difference of 2 by 2 matrices
ad − bc after combining matrices
arith_class_check: No. 33, 73, 81, 103 are all odd; 73 and 103 both prime; no class contains the key alone and the stem implies none.
one_sided_check: key largest; distractors from three error kinds (determinant split over the difference, determinant treated as linear, a sign slip). Natural errors also go over: ad + bc for 2A − B gives 143 + 40 = 183, and taking 8 − (−2) as 6 gives 143 − 24 = 119; neither is an option. Nothing in the stem says which way a slip moves a determinant.
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 73 and 81, both two-digit odd integers; neither is rounder.
cheap_bound_check: No cheap one-sided bound exists: the entries of A and B mix signs, so the size of ad and bc in 2A − B is not fixed without forming the matrix, and forming it is the work. 81 lies 22 below the key and no estimate separates them.

self_audit.note: Key largest, counters 183 and 119 go over. Each step is live alone: 3A − 2B entry (35d51f28), det(3A) (d7c66dfd); only the composition and its non-linearity trap are new.

subskill: length of the projection of one vector onto another
prompt: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, u = ⟨7, −2⟩ and v = ⟨3, 5⟩. To the nearest hundredth, what is the length of the vector projection of u onto v ?
explanation: The projection of u onto v has length |u · v|/|v|. Here u · v = 7(3) + (−2)(5) = 11 and |v| = √34 ≈ 5.831, so the length is 11/5.831 ≈ 1.89. The option 1.51 divides by |u| = √53 instead, which is the length of the projection of v onto u. The option 0.32 divides by |v|² = 34, which is the scalar multiple of v in the projection, not its length. The option 0.26 divides by |u||v|, which is the cosine of the angle between the vectors.
quantity_asked: the length of proj_v(u), the vector projection of u onto v.

distractor_kind.1.51: error path: divides the dot product by |u| (projects v onto u). (a) not a parameter extreme. (b) neighbouring problem (projection of v onto u), strictly inside (0, |u|) = (0, 7.28). (c) inside. (d) real direction-of-projection error.
distractor_kind.0.32: error path: reports (u · v)/|v|², the scalar coefficient of v, as the length. (a) no extreme. (b) not at an edge. (c) inside (0, 7.28). (d) real formula-step confusion.
distractor_kind.0.26: error path: reports the cosine (u · v)/(|u||v|). (a) no extreme. (b) not at an edge. (c) inside (0, 1) and (0, 7.28). (d) real formula confusion.

bounds: length = |u| cos θ
mechanism: vector projection length
dot product over magnitude
projection of u onto v
arith_class_check: No. Two-decimal values; nothing in the stem implies a class.
one_sided_check: key largest; the three distractors are three different formula slips. Natural errors also go over: a sign slip in the dot product (21 + 10 = 31) gives 5.32, and pairing components crosswise (7·5 − 2·3 = 29) gives 4.97, both above the key and not options. The stem does not signal a direction.
interior_parity_check: Interior by value: 0.32 and 1.51, both two decimals; neither is rounder.
cheap_bound_check: Cheapest one-sided bound: length <= |u| ≈ 7.28 (every option below it); the angle between u (about −16°) and v (about 59°) is about 75°, so a cosine estimate near 0.26 is the full computation, not a shortcut. 1.51 lies on the key's side of the 7.28 cap, 0.38 below the key.
